text:
Anika: Quick sync on hybrid model idea: use control-plane DNS for bootstrap, then publish a per-tenant VPC endpoint that becomes the canonical target. Want to surface lifecycle and failures clearly.
Rafael: I like hybrid. Two big operational risks I keep thinking about: stale caches at customer resolvers and cert rotation windows on ENIs.
Kai: For stale caches, we should use an "evented tombstone" pattern: on endpoint change, controlplane publishes a short-lived tombstone A record (ttl=10s) for 60s then repoints to new ENI. That forces re-resolution while avoiding huge DNS churn.
Priya: Tombstone idea is neat. But we must confirm registries (Route53 etc) accept tombstone semantics. Also need to avoid returning NXDOMAIN briefly because some resolvers treat that badly. Use a special tombstone IP that our connectors understand and immediately reject, prompting clients to re-resolve.
Anika: Good call — don't NXDOMAIN. Use 127.0.0.1 or a reserved ip and document that clients must treat it as signal to re-resolve.
Rafael: Security: we need a bootstrap handshake that proves we control the ENI before we mark it canonical. Proposal: two-step registration: (1) connector posts /meta with cert_fingerprint + ephemeral challenge, (2) controlplane issues short-lived bootstrap token signed, (3) connector calls /confirm with token and TLS proof. Token TTL = 300s.
security-bot: Reminder: tokens must be auditable and single-use. Log bootstrap events to kinesis for 90d retention.
Kai: Rotation semantics: support overlapping certs for X minutes. i.e., new cert deployed, connector serves both old+new for 10 min while controlplane flips canonical fingerprint. Console should show "rotating" state during that window.
Priya: Also surface a per-tenant "last_seen_fingerprint" and "last_seen_ip" in Console. Add status: pinned, canonical, tombstoned, rotating, degraded.
Anika: UX question: how do customers opt into pinning? We should allow an enterprise toggle: client_pin=true. If true, we publish a note and offer TLS pin instructions in setup docs. Default false to preserve resiliency.
Rafael: Routing priority baked into bootstrap: [eni_direct, regional_relay, public_fallback]. Connectors advertise health of eni_direct. If eni down -> controlplane marks canonical as tombstoned and flips to relay.
Kai: Implementation ops note: tombstone window should be short but measurable. We should emit metrics: tombstone_propagation_ms, stale_hit_rate, re-resolve_success_ratio. Create alert when stale_hit_rate > 1% for 30m.
Priya: For cert mismatch cases, Console should show "cert_mismatch" + a one-click "force-fallback" for support to route traffic to relay immediately. Also audit who triggers that.
ops-bot: Deploy: connector v1.3 canary scheduled Tue 02:00 UTC (2h window). Tag: canary-connector-1-3
Anika: Action items:
- Kai: prototype tombstone publish flow and metrics (tombstone_propagation_ms, stale_hit_rate).
- Rafael: draft two-step bootstrap + single-use token spec and rotation overlap policy.
- Priya: Console fields: last_seen_ip, last_seen_fingerprint, status enum (pinned, canonical, tombstoned, rotating, degraded), pinned toggle.
- Security: ensure bootstrap tokens are auditable and logged; recommend HSM signing for tokens.
Rafael: I'll sketch the RFC text for registration flow and include sequence diagrams.
Anika: Let's review the prototype at ops-sync Friday. If tombstone pattern works across major DNS providers, we can move forward with hybrid as default for new private tenants.
